correctness.rationale: Exact finite three-family partition is proved by strict transitivity of one-point extensions; the deleted-matching identity is checked independently through finite transitive closure. General finite-intensity independent omissions obey Poisson convergence and have no two edges with a common endpoint with probability tending to one, by row/column intensity bounds. The normalized correction vanishes. The known height-two formula gives a uniform normalized bound of three, permitting all fixed moment limits. An exact expected-count formula and an exponential/Markov bound prove the sharp regimes \(q_n n^2\to0\) and \(q_n n^2\to\infty\) with \(q_n\to0\). The packaged standalone checker confirms 682 finite graphs, 46 exact matching cases, 14 rational-weight expectations, and endpoints, without substituting finite tests for asymptotic proof.

originality.rationale: The final claim is a distributional result for randomly omitted height-two comparabilities, with sharp normalized-count transition, explicit non-Gaussian Poisson power, fixed moments and nonhomogeneous rare-defect universality. Direct full-text comparison with deterministic height-two one-type counts (published-finding corpus 9c2af418ff79, 828ff1d8f784) establishes that their general independent-set identity and one-deletion calculations are antecedents, not new. No checked relevant publication states or proves the random defective-parameter limit; new Poisson matching-control and out-of-window estimates are provided. However translation from classical rare-edge independent-set partition functions remains a historical priority risk, so this is provisional rather than global uniqueness certification.
residual_risks: General published finite height-two formula makes the deterministic matching specialization routine; independent originality must rest on the random distribution theorem, not that identity.
An older or unindexed independent-set partition-function Poisson theorem may imply the same distribution through the known finite identity.
No global historical-priority certification; source searches and accessible full-text readings are bounded.
The arXiv:1009.2892 and 1991 random-ordered-set primary full texts were not obtained, though their publicly available abstracts concern other scopes.

value.rationale: The finite-base logical-type count is a natural pointwise-stabilizer orbit invariant for the universal homogeneous partial order. Independent deletion of sparse cross-comparabilities creates a motivated stability question. The theorem identifies a sharp \(n^{-2}\) window, a non-Gaussian Poisson-power law and exact expectation/variance constants, plus universality under inhomogeneous local intensities. The contrast with complete-height-two type counts has genuine structural meaning; the known finite graph formula and elementary Poisson theorem are transparently credited, so value is not based on their re-derivation. The result does not claim a general random-poset limit or higher arities.
